full_judgment: 92. His Lordship Mr Justice Mustafa Kamal, (the former Chief Justice of Bangladesh) has precisely dealt with these types of questions in his book. "Bangladesh Constitution; Trends and Issues." In Chapter IX. page 159 the author wrote. "Each generation of lawyers and Judges grapple with specific issues confronting them. The entire Constitution is not thrown up for legal dissection all at a time. A Constitution unfolds itself in its beauties and deficiencies as time unfolds." In discussing the "Presumption and validity of statutes," the author has quoted the relevant portion of the judgment delivered by His Lordship Mr Justice Shahabuddin Ahmed (the former Chief Justice of Bangladesh) which says," A Constitution of Government is a living and organic thing which all instruments have the greatest claim to be construed" (reference is to Gwyer,CJ, AIR 1939 FC I in the case of Dr Nurul 1slam vs Bangladesh, 1981 BLD (AD) 140 (para 129). In Chapter- V page 85 the author wrote that "It will be important to remember that the Supreme Court of Bangladesh had very little occasion and opportunity to interpret the Constitution in its various facets and phases owing to frequent eclipse of the Constitution itself and owing to frequent interruptions with its Constitutional Jurisdiction. The Supreme Court interpreted the Constitution in fits and starts, as and when occasion permitted. The development of Constitutional law in Bangladesh was thwarted in its infancy. But looking at the crop of Constitutional cases which sprang up during the interlude (1979-82) one can safely conclude that had the Supreme Court been left free to do its work uninterruptedly the Constitution would have received a much more comprehensive and intensive interpretation in its hands." To trace the historical background as to how the development of Constitutional law in Bangladesh was thwarted in its infancy the author wrote, "The Constitution (Fourth Amendment) Act, 1975 made the first surgery on the powers of the High Court Division. Its power under Article 102(1) to issue directions. Orders, etc. for enforcement of fundamental rights was taken away, gone was the fundamental right to move the High Court Division for enforcement of fundamental rights under Article 44. Fundamental rights were to be enforced (in future) by a Constitutional Court. Tribunal or Commission which may be established by parliament by law (page 34). The Fourth Amendment came into force on the 25th January 1975. A new Part VIA was inserted in the Constitution, providing for the formation of a National Party to the exclusion of all other parties. Bangladesh Krishak Sramik Awami League was formed in pursuance of this Constitutional provision. The District Administration Act, 1975 was enacted on the 10th July, 1975 for the administration of districts along totalitarian lines. All newspapers and periodicals except a designated few lost their declaration by the newspapers (Amendment of Declaration) Act. 1975 made on the 19th July, 1975. Multiple political parties and independent newspapers and periodicals lost their existence before Martial Law was proclaimed on the 15th August, 1975 (page-55-56).
